highlights.title: Musicians-turned-detectives are hunting for AI grifters
highlights.summary: As audio-focused generative tools and platforms have gotten more sophisticated, the internet has become increasingly filled with AI-generated music whose melodies and vocals are algorithmically derived from the work of human artists.
body: As AI infiltrates the electronic dance music scene, a callout culture is brewing.

For musicians — especially those creating art in technologically-focused spaces like electronic dance music — the increasingly complicated question of what is “real” and what isn’t feels particularly urgent and personal. Professional courtesy can make this only more complex; listeners can call out performers they suspect of using gen AI, but it’s something else for artists to raise concerns about their professional peers. There are some though, like 26-year-old EDM producer Max “H4RRIS” Harris, who are taking a stand against generative technology with videos calling out anyone they believe is trying to pass off AI slop as human-made art.

When I recently spoke with Harris, he told me that he sees AI-generated music as “a kind of decoy art form,” and he thinks that the people making it don’t really have anything meaningful to say with their creations. He feels that true art in any medium is “created by people that are trying to express feelings and messages,” and he believes that the only thing AI boosters are really interested in is making a quick profit.

The promising 22-year-old clinched his second trophy of the season having lifted his maiden tour-level trophy at the ATP 500 event in Hamburg.
Fery was aiming to add to his already memorable season having reached the semi-finals at Wimbledon and he is set for a new career high Monday.
With his spot in the Winston-Salem final, 24-year-old Fery has moved up to a new career high of No 33 in the live rankings, overtaking Cameron Norrie as the British No 1 in doing so.

highlights.title: Relive Nintendo's wild Donkey Kong court case from 1983
highlights.summary: If you're a gaming history buff, then you likely know all about the landmark 1983 Universal case in which Nintendo had to defend the right to keep using Donkey Kong. Decades later, King Kong is thriving (and BFFs with Godzilla ), and both entertainment giants are happily collaborating on the box…
body: Gaming Historian is a YouTuber known for producing extensively researched documentaries that some fans compare to Ken Burns. In early April, citing burnout, the personality saddened fans by announcing that he would no longer make educational videos about retro games. To mark the occasion, the YouTuber left fans a parting gift in the form of a document dump.

The collection is the paper trail for the Universal vs. Nintendo case in its entirety. We're talking about everything from the evidence presented in the proceedings to logs of the witness interrogations. Nintendo argued that its ditsy gorilla was not influenced by the other famous gorilla of that time, King Kong, because the franchise actually began as a licensed adaptation of Popeye the Sailor Man.
Here, Miyamoto was asked what other names he considered for Donkey Kong. His answer? "The names which were in my mind." Honestly, iconic.
You can read the full Miyamoto deposition here, or check out the larger document trove here.

highlights.title: “We’re not doing 30 bets a year”: Vijay Pande on betting small after running $4 billion at a16z
highlights.summary: Vijay Pande — who left a16z's roughly $4 billion biotech practice last year to start the much smaller, AI-native VZVC — talks about why biology is finally shifting from a "discovery" science to an "engineering" one, why clinical trials are still brutally expensive, and why he thinks open, shared…
body: It used to be that Vijay Pande was better known in academic circles than investor circles. That changed pretty abruptly a dozen years ago, when Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz — who’d spent their firm’s first five years explicitly avoiding healthcare and life sciences — decided the category was worth betting on after all and handed the keys to Pande. At the time, he was a Stanford chemistry professor who was best known for building Folding@home, the distributed-computing project that turned millions of home PCs into a supercomputer for disease research. Over the next decade-plus, he grew a16z’s bet into a practice managing close to $4 billion.

So it was somewhat unexpected when in June of last year, Pande walked away from it all to start something much smaller. In fact, his new firm, VZVC, co-founded with longtime investor Zach Werner, is built around a handful of concentrated bets a year rather than dozens, it has no associates, and it relies heavily on AI for its day-to-day operations.

body: Hovland produced a birdie-birdie finish to post a five-under 65 at East Lake, lifting the 2023 FedExCup champion to 15 under and with a narrow advantage over playing partner Ryan Gerard.

The halfway co-leaders were chased down by a star-studded chasing pack during a thrilling Saturday at the PGA Tour's season finale, with world no 1 Scottie Scheffler three shots back in third spot and chasing a second FedExCup title.

Scheffler is joined on 12 under by Chris Gotterup, Adam Scott and Ludvig Åberg, who produced a three-birdie finish to his third-round 65, as McIlroy jumped to tied-seventh after setting the early clubhouse target with a round-of-the-day 63.
McIlroy sits five strokes back alongside Cameron Young as he searches for a record-extending fourth FedExCup title, with all 29 players in the field under-par heading into the final round.

highlights.title: Baldur's Gate 3's Astarion Is Getting an Official Prequel Novel
highlights.summary: The world of Larian Studios' Baldur's Gate 3 is expanding. The wildly successful 2023 RPG set in the Dungeons & Dragons universe was the first to claim Game of the Year honors at all five major award ceremonies.
body: Baldur’s Gate 3: Astarion, written by the award-winning, New York Times bestselling fantasy author T. Kingfisher, will hit stores on Sept. 29. This prequel novel, published by Random House Worlds, takes place prior to the events of the 2023 game, and follows the fan-favorite High Elf during his years of servitude under the vampire lord Cazador Szarr. Baldur's Gate 3 senior writer Stephen Rooney consulted on the project in order to ensure consistency with the game's lore and world-building. An audiobook narrated by Neil Newbon — who took home the trophy for Best Performance for his portrayal of Astarion at The Game Awards in 2023 — will also be published by Penguin Random House Audio.

In July, Clarkson Potter published Baldur’s Gate 3: The Necromancy of Thay, a blank, grid-paper notebook that faithfully reproduces a key in-game item. It features foil stamping, an embossed skull on the cover, and illustrated "clasps" to keep its unholy contents out of the wrong hands. In August, Ten Speed Press published The Official Baldur's Gate 3 Coloring Book. It includes 40 black-and-white line drawings of characters, settings, and creatures from the game, with illustrations by Jaki King.

highlights.title: Vicariously hike the Appalachian in the gorgeous A Trail Tale
highlights.summary: I used to be an avid hiker and would try to go backpacking a few times a year. I always dreamed of thru-hiking the Appalachian Trail, but life kind of got in the way. (Turns out jobs, wives, and children aren't thrilled with the idea of you disappearing for three months.) But I've been longing to…
body: It’s an interactive trail journal inspired by Sierra point-and-click adventures and Oregon Trail.

The various segments of the trail are rendered in beautiful pixel art reminiscent of a ‘90s Sierra point-and-click adventure. Alex recorded an equally gorgeous original score that combines nature sounds, acoustic guitar, strings, and even what sounds like clarinet.

As you click through each day, you’re greeted with information about landmarks and a game-like UI that is partially inspired by titles like Oregon Trail. (Spoiler: nobody dies of dysentery in this one.) Clicking on Andy unfurls a menu of icons that offer details about the journey, his mental state, and even bits of poetry. There are even little icons for things that impact his fortitude and morale meters, like inclement weather or picturesque scenery.
It’s insanely easy to just get lost in Andy’s journey for hours. And it’s making me wonder if I should get back out there and start tackling some more of the AT myself.

highlights.title: How to Run a Chatbot on Your Own Computer
highlights.summary: Installing a large language model on your personal computer gives you a handy digital assistant that won’t compromise your data privacy.
body: It's no exaggeration to say the large language models that power AI bots like ChatGPT and Gemini are changing the world. Many of us are now relying on them for coding, writing, summarizing, and searching the web. Whatever directions AI goes in over the next few years, LLMs will be part of that future.

If you use ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, or any of the other AI platforms, then you're using an LLM. What's less commonly known is that these LLMs can be run locally, on your own computer. The key benefits are offline access and greater privacy, because you're not sending anything to the cloud for anyone else to analyze or review.

You're also not paying any AI companies a monthly subscription or hitting any usage rates. Numerous LLMs are available to download for free, including from big names like Meta and Google. Though they tend not to be as advanced or as speedy as the LLMs inside the apps you have to pay for, they're capable enough for everyday use, and you can pick and choose between them as needed.

highlights.title: Netflix's New 10-Part Mystery Thriller Is a Perfect Weekend Binge From Start to Finish
highlights.summary: Paranormal procedural shows are a dime a dozen. From The X-Files to iZombie, the genre spans decades and has something for everyone, whether you’re a hardcore horror sicko or someone who enjoys the spooky vibes and character dynamics that can pop up in these hyper-realized scenarios.
body: It’s a winning formula, which is why the genre has become so crowded. But if you’ve seen all of the classics and want a supernatural story anchored by a genuinely engaging family drama — with a fresh twist on the zombie trope — you’re in luck. The first season of Syfy’s 2025 series Revival is now streaming on Netflix.

Created by Aaron B. Koontz and Luke Boyce, and based on the comic series by Tim Seeley and Mike Norton, Revival follows a family in crisis in the small town of Wausau, Wisconsin. Dana Cypress (Melanie Scrofano) is a divorced cop who's desperate to leave the town she’s been trapped in her entire life. She’s finalizing a move to Chicago and plans on leaving with her son (Hudson Robert Wurster) for a fresh start as soon as her transfer is approved. Her boss, as it turns out, is her father and the town’s Sheriff (David James Elliott) — someone worth trusting in a crisis, yet not the most pleasant person to be around 24/7.

highlights.summary: Michael Kutryk, the owner of the now-famous cabin featured in “Heated Rivalry” Season 1, said he needed to do some “soul searching” before allowing the HBO production to come back for Season 2. “I did a little bit of soul searching about allowing them to come back,” Kutryk told HGTV.
body: Kutryk’s house was featured in the “Heated Rivalry” Season 1 finale, titled “The Cottage,” in which Shane Hollander ( Hudson Williams ) brings Ilya Rozanov ( Connor Storrie ) to his remote family cabin for a private getaway. Kutryk, a Toronto doctor, said he was shocked when he first listened to Rachel Reid’s “Game Changer,” on which the show is based, on audiobook.

“My jaw just dropped as I listened. The pretty explicit nature of the book made me wonder just what they’d be filming … and showing!” Kutryk said. “I just thought, OK, they’re gonna film what they’re gonna film. What’s done is done.”

“We’ll see after Season 2 airs what demand is like,” he added. “It’s still true: I’m a private guy. This is my retreat. I built this to get away from the world, so I don’t know how much longer I’ll continue to share it.”

“Heated Rivalry” Season 2, which was greenlit in December 2025, is expected to release in April 2027. highlights.title: Addisu Gobena smashes Sydney Marathon record as Jepchirchir wins fourth women’s major
highlights.summary: Ethiopian former javelin thrower claims men’s race in 2hr 4min 42sec. Kenyan adds harbourside crown to Boston, New York and London titles. Ethiopia’s Addisu Gobena surged to a record-breaking victory in the men’s race at the Sydney Marathon, while Kenya’s Peres Jepchirchir claimed the women’s crown…
body: In perfect conditions, Gobena won the hotly contested men’s race in two hours four minutes and 42 seconds – more than a minute and a half quicker than the previous record on the hilly harbourside course which attracted 40,000 competitors from around the world.

The 21-year-old Ethiopian, who was a javelin thrower until 2023, broke away with compatriot Chimdessa Debele Gudeta from the lead pack of six runners inside the final two kilometres and then surged ahead on the downhill finish to the Sydney Opera House to win by four seconds.

Gobena, who finished second behind Hailemaryam Kiros last year, celebrated by punching the air after crossing the finish line. “I am very happy. Last year I came second, I learned from my mistake, and I went back home and I worked on my mistake to perform and break the record today,” said Gobena through an interpreter.
Lesotho’s Tebello Ramakongoana was third in 2:04:57. The top seven finishers, including Kiros, were all inside Kiros’ record time of 2:06:06 set in last year’s race.

highlights.title: GTA 6 Will Have No Microtransactions or Generative AI at Launch, Rockstar Says
highlights.summary: Rockstar Games has said Grand Theft Auto 6 will have no microtransactions or generative AI when it launches in November. The studio behind GTA 6 confirmed this year's monumental open-world game will dodge two potentially controversial practices during a conversation with Kinda Funny Games earlier…
body: Kinda Funny's Andy Cortez said he asked Rockstar if players will be able to use real-world money to purchase things in-game during a preview event that preceded the GTA 6: Extended Look. He went on, saying, "no monetizations in this game."
The site's Greg Miller immediately followed that topic, saying he asked Rockstar "point-blank" if there is generative AI in GTA 6. The team told him that there is "no AI" used in the game.

From Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 to Arc Raiders, generative AI has proven time and time again to be an especially troublesome element for developers to include in their games. The millions of gamers who have waited 13 years for the next Grand Theft Auto might be pleased to hear similar claims won't mar its mid-November release date. The issue of microtransactions, however, does come with a few things worth noting.

highlights.title: Heidi Montag Recalls Dolly Parton Defending Her Amid Plastic Surgery Criticism
highlights.summary: "When I was at one of the hardest and most criticized moment of my life after my plastic surgery, Dolly was one of the only people in the industry who didn't take the opportunity to drag me down," 'The Hills' shared on X.
body: Heidi Montag is remembering the kindness the late Dolly Parton showed her during one of the most heavily criticized periods of her life.
Following news of Parton’s death earlier this week, Montag took to X on Friday night to pay tribute to the country music legend, recalling how Parton defended her after she underwent plastic surgery.
According to Montag, she recalled that Parton said at the time, “I had probably done the same thing if I was her age and could afford it, if I thought I needed it.”

In 2009, Montag famously underwent 10 plastic surgery procedures in one day, including breast augmentation, a nose job revision and chin reduction. She faced intense scrutiny over the procedures, with the aftermath documented on The Hills, including a heartbreaking scene in which she revealed her new appearance to her mother.

highlights.title: Alt-right troll Milo Yiannopoulos has been deported
highlights.summary: Alt-right troll Milo Yiannopoulos was arrested by ICE on Thursday, and today the Department of Homeland Security confirmed to Reuters and the Washington Post that he had been deported to the UK. Yiannopoulos came to the US legally in 2019, but overstayed his visa.
body: The controversial Gamergate figure has been sent back to the UK after overstaying his visa.

The British national made a name for himself as an editor at Steve Bannon’s Breitbart and an early supporter of Donald Trump’s. He has had a long history of controversial statements and associations, including reportedly helping arrange Trump’s dinner with Kanye West and white nationalist Nick Fuentes, and he was a key figure in the online harassment campaign Gamergate.

In recent years, however, his antics have led to a falling out with most significant figures on the right, including MAGA influencer Laura Loomer. He has denied condoning statutory rape or pedophilia, but he has suggested it’s acceptable for an adult to have a sexual relationship with a 13-year-old.
There’s no word if the 44 interns in a trenchcoat who also constitute the entity known as Milo Yiannopoulos have also been deported.

highlights.title: Nvidia’s AI advantage is moving beyond the GPU
highlights.summary: The new generation of data center systems is increasing efficiency with smarter traffic control instead of just more processor cycles.
body: Before this week, the dominant story about Nvidia went something like this: For the first few years of the AI boom, Nvidia was the only source for state-of-the-art GPUs, which became immensely profitable as the industry scaled out. In the last few years, hyperscalers like Amazon and Google have started building their own chips, and Nvidia is no longer the only game in town, leading many investors to wonder how durable its advantage really is.

It’s a compelling story, and mostly true. After growing its market cap 10x between the start of 2023 and mid-2025, Nvidia shares have been on a more modest trajectory for the past year, driven by concerns about GPU competition.

A new narrative has taken shape since the company’s earnings on Wednesday and investors are starting to realize that Nvidia’s advantage goes far beyond GPUs. As AI’s compute grows into the gigawatt scale, orchestration has become an increasingly complex task. Not surprisingly, Nvidia has built much of the state-of-the-art hardware needed to handle it, giving the company a huge advantage in the systems that surround the GPU even as it sees increased competition on the GPUs themselves.
points: The new generation of data center systems is increasing efficiency with smarter traffic control instead of just more processor cycles.

highlights.title: Doom Meets Hades In the Coolest New Action Game of Gamescom 2026
highlights.summary: If you play video games, you’ve probably internalized an automatic association without even realizing it: see isometric, think roguelike. Murals, a new action game from the makers of Disney Illusion Island, bucks that trend.
body: Revealed at the 2026 Gamescom Opening Night Live showcase, Murals is the next game from Dlala Studios, the British-based developer that also gave us 2020’s beat-em-up revival of Battletoads. Murals is a deviation from both of its hits: an isometric, narrative-forward action game. But it is not, as CEO and game director Aj Grand-Scutton was quick to tell me during a hands-off preview at Gamescom, a roguelike. Don’t expect a one-to-one Hades clone here, folks.

During the Gamescom demo, Dlala Studios showed off Murals ’ fifth chapter, in which The Hero enters a beachy, aquatic realm based on The Little Mermaid. (Loaf chimes in: “This mural’s gonna be a beach, am I right?”) When you enter a combat chamber, walls go up, trapping you in that room until you defeat all of the enemies in the area. You can attack them close up with a quick-slashing sword or a lumbering, powerful hammer, and have ranged attacks as well. It’s a fast-paced, dash-based game, too: Forget parrying, you’ll zip around the arena dodging enemy attacks.

highlights.title: Sony Music and Warner Chappell are suing Anthropic
highlights.summary: Sony Music and Warner Chappell have filed suit against Anthropic in the US District Court for the Northern District of California seeking damages for "tens of thousands" copyrighted works.
body: The companies call it “one of the largest and most blatant ongoing thefts of intellectual property in history.”

This is just the latest high-profile suit against Anthropic, which recently settled a suit brought by the publishing industry for $1.5 billion. It’s also faced multiple lawsuits from Universal Music Group, Concord, and ABKCO, plus separate suits from BMG and Round Hill Music.

In addition to suing Anthropic as an entity, the complaint names Co-Founders Dario Amodei and Benjamin Mann as individual defendants. The suit alleges that Mann used BitTorrent to download over five million pirated books, and that employees downloaded at least two million more from Pirate Library Mirror. It also claims that Anthropic scraped lyrics from sites like MusixMatch and LyricFind, which paid to license content from the labels.

highlights.title: Filip Hrgovic stuns Britain’s Moses Itauma to claim IBF world heavyweight title
highlights.summary: 21-year-old Itauma stopped after ninth-round rally. 34-year-old Hrgovic is first Croat to win such a title. Moses Itauma’s hopes of becoming the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in history lay in ruins after the extraordinarily tough and resilient Filip Hrgovic stopped him in the ninth…
body: The fight changed course when Itauma’s stamina suddenly dipped and he began to weave in woozy fatigue as Hrgovic fought back with granite-like determination. Itauma could not withstand the dark storm rolling over him in the ninth and he sank back against the ropes as Hrgovic opened up with renewed conviction. Just as the referee stepped in to stop the fight, Ben Davison, Itauma’s trainer, also sent a white towel sailing sadly over the listing ropes to save his man from a knockout.

The shocking twist was too much for the 21-year-old and he left the ring on a stretcher, apparently having injured his knee. But the damage was done by the remarkable fightback from his opponent, who made his own significant slice of boxing history. The admirable Hrgovic is the first world heavyweight champion from Croatia – a country that has no real boxing heritage.

highlights.title: Trump’s EPA wants to let data centers hide their air pollution
highlights.summary: Just as new data centers face growing backlash from neighboring communities, the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is about to make it harder for people to weigh in on any pollution those centers create.
body: The Trump administration wants to scrap another federal air pollution rule. Advocates say it’ll help data center developers avoid public scrutiny.

The EPA plans to toss out a federal rule requiring public notice and an opportunity to comment when certain industrial sites apply for an air permit. Advocates warn that the move would allow data center developers and other industries to break ground without giving nearby residents a say, or even a warning that construction is planned.

“You can see why that would be so interesting to an administration that wants to rush through the construction of data centers,” says Keri Powell, senior attorney and air program leader at the Southern Environmental Law Center (SELC). “What EPA would be allowing would be all of those facilities to go through and just not have to deal with the public, issue the permits in secret behind closed doors. Nobody knows what’s happening until the bulldozers are out there.”

highlights.title: ‘It gives Shein’: how did polyester become the world’s most-hated material?
highlights.summary: Due to its ubiquity in fast fashion, gen Z are pushing back against the synthetic material and using it as an insult. In 2015, Kate Moss called an easyJet pilot a “basic bitch” and a catchy new insult meaning obvious and uncool hit the mainstream.
body: But its use as a figurative insult also echoes a literal backlash against polyester, now the most-produced synthetic fibre on the planet.

In gyms, the pilates princess aesthetic with its synthetic matching sets is waning while 1990s-style exercise gear is becoming fashionable once more as many lionize exercise garments displaying visible sweat – think Sylvester Stallone in Rocky, or John Travolta being sweatily hypnotized by Jamie Lee Curtis’s rocking pelvis in the 1985 movie Perfect.

Some of the pushback centres around polyester’s impact on the planet. Derived from fossil fuels, it does not biodegrade, and sheds microplastics when washed. Many anti-polyester influencers, however, talk about giving up the fabric in the same way they might talk about giving up sugar, sharing content with hashtags such as #naturalfibers, #antipolyester and #nontoxicclothing while posting videos of large shopping hauls of cotton and linen from Zara.

highlights.title: How to save money on your phone bill with an MVNO
highlights.summary: There are wireless providers offering plans at a fraction of the cost you'll find at major carriers like AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon.
body: Using a popular postpaid plan with one of the three major phone carriers (AT&T, T-Mobile or Verizon) isn't cheap. Most of them cost at least $50 per month and can get close to $100/month for a single person. You have to join the priciest plans to take advantage of many "on us" phone deals, and they frequently inflate the cost with bundled extras you might not even use.

Thankfully, these carriers aren't your only option. There's a whole fleet of low-cost mobile providers, known as mobile virtual network operators (MVNOs), that provide reliable service for a fraction of the price. I've been using these services for over a decade and would recommend them to pretty much everyone.

The big carriers like Verizon and AT&T are officially known as mobile network operators (MNOs). They're the businesses that control all the infrastructure involved in making cell connections happen, like towers and radio access networks. In contrast, MVNOs are "virtual" because they run a network without owning any of what powers it. These companies lease huge amounts of access from the network operators, then sell it to customers at lower rates.
points: There are wireless providers offering plans at a fraction of the cost you'll find at major carriers like AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon.
